title: Group Education, Research on Knowledge Levels and Information Sources (including AI etc.) and Clinical Evaluation in the Menopausal Transition a) Evaluation of a group-based information and diagnostic concept for peri- and postmenopausal patients in a university hormone clinic b) Evaluation of the assessment of knowledge about symptoms, pathomechanisms, and treatment options for menopause, as well as the use of information sources, in particular AI, among peri- and postmenopausal patients
summary:
Women in peri- and postmenopause often experience psychological and physical symptoms that can significantly impair their quality of life, ability to work, and productivity. Despite good treatment options, especially hormone therapy, which often has a favorable risk-benefit profile when used early, there is a significant gap in care and a considerable lack of information among affected patients in Germany. The new concept of the Menopause Information Day (MIT) at the University Women's Hospital addresses this knowledge and care gap through a group-based approach. During each information day, up to 30 patients are first given a joint briefing on the causes, symptoms, and treatment options for menopause, followed by a 25-minute individual consultation/examination.
 
The aim of this observational study is to evaluate this new care format (process evaluation, acceptance, and feasibility), the increase in knowledge about symptoms and treatment options, and the use of information sources. This is done both through questionnaires and interviews with individual participants. Those conducting the MIT will also be interviewed. In addition, the initial burden and the importance of nutritional medicine will be assessed, and a correlation between knowledge assessment and psychological symptoms will be analyzed. A survey on symptoms, therapies, and nutritional medicine will also be conducted after 3 months.

interventions.name: As part of this prospective observational study, participants in a menopause information day (MIT) will be asked to evaluate the MIT concept on a one-time basis. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion criteria (participants): Adult patients; participation in the Menopause Information Day; completed medical history forms; written consent
Inclusion criteria (researchers): Participation in the Menopause Information Day; written consent
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria (participants): refusal to participate in the study by patients; lack of consent; patients who are legally incapable of giving consent; insufficient understanding of the German language; patients under the age of 18
Exclusion criteria (researchers): refusal to participate in the study; lack of consent; employees under the age of 18
